analysis_options.bank_phase: raw PcodeOpBank create/markAlive/destroy and public target
analysis_options.split_phase: direct FlowInfo::splitBasic on four raw ops
analysis_options.flow_phase: production SLEIGH oneInstruction via FlowInfo::generateOps then generateBlocks

input.flow_run_relationship: three independent production runs; never represented as one combined visited map

comparand.snapshot_scope: entire tracked tree at the verified pinned_base_commit/tree; C++/Rust fixtures, metadata, and runner are captured once as validated overlays, and only the Rust fixture enters the Rugra source compilation

decisive_semantics.references_outputs: Op identities are pointer/Arc identities labeled once; target and parent fields refer back to those identities. FlowInfo, PcodeOpBank, BlockGraph, and call vectors retain their production alias relationships.
decisive_semantics.iteration_boundaries_order: Creation order, SeqNum natural optree order, alive/dead list order, visited-map order, block order, and per-block op order are emitted without sorting away semantic order. lower_bound candidates and final bank targets are separate fields.
decisive_semantics.counters_accumulators: PcodeOpBank uniq starts at zero and increments per create; SeqNum time is immutable; pre-block Ghidra order is explicitly UNINITIALIZED rather than read; post-insert mutable order, instruction count, visited count, and block ordinals are observed.
decisive_semantics.sort_comparison_keys: Address ordering is space index then offset; SeqNum optree ordering is Address then time; equal-offset RAM/stack/overlay and equal-address R0/R1 provide both primary and tie-break cases.

cases.detail: All six cross-space lower_bound candidates and final public bank targets match with full space name/index/offset identity.
Ghidra create starts dead with an uninitialized mutable order; Rugra create starts alive and initializes order from time. R1::target also walks in the opposite direction.
Ghidra throws LowlevelError:Deleting integrated op and preserves membership; Rugra destroys the alive op.
After split, block count/entry ordinal, op identity, parent ordinal, within-block op order, and mutable SeqNum order all match.
Ghidra records one-space RangeList covers and derives entry/start/stop from them; Rugra exposes no entry/cover, drops start space, and approximates stop from the last op.
Ghidra throws before mutation; Rugra emits a warning and constructs one block.

Production generation reaches the same instruction/block cardinalities, but Rugra loses space identity from generated ops, visited snapshots, and block range state and uses the opposite raw alive/dead phase.
Ghidra retains overlay visited/op identities then throws when the x86 RAM branch target has no overlay-owned op; Rugra erases the tag and completes two blocks.
Ghidra retains stack visited/op identities then throws when the x86 RAM branch target has no stack-owned op; Rugra erases the tag and completes two blocks.
The public Rust API cannot place RAM, overlay, and stack entries into one FlowInfo visited map or invoke private newAddress directly; three independent runs are not reported as a combined state.
